findings_agree.queue: Q*L is the current numerical configuration check, not a cap on the two retained Vec capacities in each queued ControllerJob.
findings_agree.arithmetic: Q=2/L=1024 allows budget 2048 bytes; Q jobs with both Vec capacities at least L occupy at least 4096 bytes. Defaults Q=64/L=8 MiB give 512 MiB versus at least 1 GiB.
findings_agree.lifetimes: One active owner is additional to Q queued jobs; successful oneshot replies can retain response/request allocations in caller futures after the queue drains. Caller-owned unpolled futures and transport buffers are separately scoped.
findings_agree.network: The source allows direct callers to provide large capacities; no remotely triggerable allocation size or exploit has been demonstrated.

details: A unit test within protocol.rs can create a handler around a test-owned bounded receiver and poll submit once, leaving its oneshot pending while inspecting queued ControllerJob buffers.
For the two-buffer Q*L check, enqueue Q jobs first, then drain and retain them together while inspecting their actual Vec capacities and pointers.
Add both-sum and individual-overcapacity controls, queue-full/stopped/error precedence, checked arithmetic, response/reuse behavior, and a separately gated real-actor journal comparison.
No approach that only caps each vector independently at L establishes a Q*L queue-capacity bound.

limits: No Rust compilation, native test, actor/WAL execution, real network, benchmark or publication.
This validates a source finding and a test design; no fix or production-readiness claim is established.
